task: DAEO-03ub (W2-42a), read-only here-string forms with an expanded text stay free (DEC-1164 (18), R3 F1)
status: done. The 21 red acceptance cases are green, and nothing that was green turned red.
work_completed:
- The change is in `_check_here_strings` in `src/gov/guard/bash_writes.py`. The first reading used to give up on any here-string whose reader was not in `_DATA`. It now counts the here-string's reader as data in these cases:
  - `read`, `mapfile`, `readarray` and `bc`, whatever the text.
  - `sed` or `awk` whose script writes and runs nothing. `_sed_reads_only` scans the script command by command. It refuses `-i`, `-f`, any `w`/`W`/`e` command, an `s` flag `w` or `e`, and anything it does not understand. `_awk_reads_only` refuses `system`, `>`, `|`, `getline`, `inplace`, `close`, `fflush`, `-f`, `-i`, `-l` and `-E`.
  - `done` of a loop, when no command anywhere in the call reads its input as code. The loop body is then judged by its own words.
- Every other reader keeps R3's fail-closed fallback: `bash`/`sh`/`zsh`/`dash`, `xargs`, `source`, `eval`, any unnamed reader, a writing `sed`/`awk` script, and a loop with a stdin-runner in it.
- A `$(…)` in the text is still judged as a command, so its writes stay targets.
- I did not change `decide.py`.
- I did not read the acceptance tests. I worked from the failure output in the brief.
files_changed: `src/gov/guard/bash_writes.py`; `tests/unit/guard/test_w2_42a_here_string_ro.py` (new, 64 cases); `docs/changes/W2-42a-evidence.md` (one paragraph).
evidence:
- `tests/acceptance/W2-42a` with `tests/unit/guard`, first run: `1670 passed, 2 xfailed in 27.36s`.
- Same with `tests/unit/hooks` added, final run: `2 failed, 1930 passed, 2 xfailed in 29.40s`.
- The builder file on its own: `64 passed`. Against the unfixed `bash_writes.py` it gave `31 failed, 33 passed`.
- The 2 failures are `test_live_hook.py::test_a_catastrophic_rm_is_refused[outside the project]` and `::test_the_reason_is_plain`. Both fail on `rm -f ~/.bashrc` being allowed under the scratch HOME. They fail the same with the old `bash_writes.py`, and the evidence file already records them as failing on the base.
tests:
- The new builder file covers four groups:
  - 16 read-only forms that give no target.
  - 8 templates where a write beside the form, or a `$(…)` in the text, still gives its target.
  - 20 forms that stay unresolvable: shells, xargs, source, eval, a pipe into `sh`, an unknown reader, writing `sed`/`awk` scripts, a loop body with `bash` or `xargs`, and `{ read; } <<<`.
  - The two script scanners tested directly.
- The DEC-409 lift cases in `tests/unit/pause`, `tests/unit/containment`, `tests/unit/guard/test_decide.py`, `test_w2_42a_apos2.py` and `tests/acceptance/W1-28` were not run on their own.
  - The ones in `tests/unit/guard` and `tests/acceptance/W2-42a` ran in the full runs and passed.
  - The `-k` exclusion (`real`, `green_here`, `time_limit`) and `-m "not local_only"` left out the real-model cases, as the brief says. I did not run `tests/unit/pause`, `tests/unit/containment` or `tests/acceptance/W1-28`.
discoveries:
- In the first reading, quoted here-strings of data readers already worked. The expanded ones failed because `_check_here_strings` raised `Unreadable`, and the `hstr` fallback then made the unresolvable target.
- A here-string on `sed` with a quoted text now takes the text as data in the first reading. Before, the fallback judged the text as commands. That follows rule 3, and the acceptance cases that refuse R3's forms stay green.
risks:
- The loop rule judges the body by its own words, as decided. It only refuses a loop when the call contains a shell, Python, `xargs`, `parallel`, `source`, `eval`, `perl`, `node`, `ruby` or `php` reader. An unlisted program that reads stdin and runs it (`ssh`, `docker exec -i`) in a loop body, with a here-string on `done`, is no longer refused. Before this change the fallback judged the text as commands.
- `_awk_reads_only` is deliberately conservative. A comparison like `$1 > 5` counts as a possible redirect and falls back to R3's rule, as it did before.
lessons: The brief's "grep tests for DEC-409" shows the lift cases are spread over several folders, so a run limited to `tests/unit/guard` and the acceptance folder does not cover all of them.
